name: Finite groups of order < 60 are solvable

source.question: Can the general theorem 'finite group of order < 60 is solvable' be formalized?

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Proved p-group→solvable chain and abelian→solvable using Mathlib. Documented complete order classification below 60. Full theorem needs Burnside p^a·q^b (not in Mathlib). 0A/0S, 4 proved theorems, 104 lines.
builtItems: Complete order classification table by proof method
insights: IsNilpotent.to_isSolvable is an instance, use infer_instance
Burnside p^a·q^b is the main missing piece for 33 of 59 orders
Only 2 orders (30, 42) have ≥ 3 distinct prime factors below 60
mathlibGaps: Burnside's p^a · q^b theorem (requires character theory or transfer)
IsSolvable instance for Perm (Fin n) for n ≤ 4 not easily accessible
nextSteps: Prove Burnside's p^a·q^b theorem in Mathlib
Or: case-by-case Sylow counting for remaining 33 orders
Connect to Feit-Thompson (odd order theorem) for odd orders
